Advances: specled.spec_review

Orchestrated under epic specled_-233 (2026-07-26), shipping on one PR with specled_-48i, specled_-vk0, specled_-ymn. Reparented here from specled_-xkn, whose other three children (26g, xkn.1, xkn.2) stay there; this ticket's `lib/**` precondition is now satisfied.

## Context

Follow-up to specled_-q6l.5 (split over-compound spec_review.coverage_tab_bind_closure requirement). That ticket added 8 new per-contract requirement ids under specled.spec_review (coverage_closure_line_format, coverage_reached_by_tests_per_test_only, coverage_observed_approximate_qualifier, coverage_file_level_proxy_qualifier, coverage_rollup_badge, coverage_generated_at_staleness, coverage_degraded_banners_distinct, coverage_no_tracer_manifest_banner), each with its own scenario and named covering test in test/specled_ex/review/html_test.exs.

It deliberately left the original compound requirement id and full statement UNCHANGED (not shrunk to a pointer, not removed) because `lib/**` was out of scope there, and covers comments in `lib/**` must keep resolving to a known requirement id per the SpecLedEx.Verifier file-content covers check. Editing or removing the id without repointing those comments would break LINKED-strength file-kind verification or leave dangling references.

This ticket: repoint those covers comments to the appropriate new split ids, and either delete the now-redundant compound requirement or shrink it to a short umbrella/pointer sentence, removing the prose duplication between the compound statement and its 8 children.

## Pre-flight correction (orchestrator, 2026-07-26) — the marker inventory above is INCOMPLETE

The context says three lib files. At base 402f4a27 the real inventory is FOUR lib files carrying SIX markers, plus four test-file markers. Repointing only three would leave three dangling references in lib/specled_ex/review.ex. Full inventory of `# covers: specled.spec_review.coverage_tab_bind_closure`:

- lib/specled_ex/review.ex:56
- lib/specled_ex/review.ex:65
- lib/specled_ex/review.ex:772
- lib/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation.ex:162
- lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex:2756
- lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex:2
- test/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation_test.exs:330
- test/specled_ex/review_test.exs:303
- test/specled_ex/review/html_test.exs:1128
- test/specled_ex/review/html_test.exs:1390 (compound line, also covers coverage_tab_v2_envelope_data_layer)

And in .spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md the id appears at line 258 (the requirement itself), line 423 (a prose cross-reference inside ANOTHER requirement's statement — update it or it becomes a dangling prose reference), and as a `covers:` entry in six verification entries at lines 772, 861, 896, 948, 961, 965.

Re-derive this inventory yourself (`grep -rn coverage_tab_bind_closure .spec/ lib/ test/`) — do not trust either list blindly. Repoint each marker to the split id whose contract that specific call site actually implements. A blanket repoint of all six lib markers to one id is a rubber stamp and will bounce.

## Allowed touches

- `.spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md` — the coverage_tab_bind_closure requirement (delete, or shrink to a short umbrella/pointer sentence), the line-423 prose cross-reference, and the six verification `covers:` lists.
- `lib/specled_ex/review.ex`, `lib/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation.ex`, `lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex`, `lib/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure.ex` — covers-comment repointing ONLY, no behavior change.
- `test/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation_test.exs`, `test/specled_ex/review_test.exs`, `test/specled_ex/review/html_test.exs` — covers-comment repointing.
- `.spec/realization_hashes.json` — via its documented regeneration command, if the spec gate demands it.

Co-changing the `Advances:` subject spec above IS authorized: a green `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` outranks a narrow reading of Out of Scope. Do NOT weaken a requirement to make code pass.

## Out of Scope (files)

- `.spec/specs/spec_review.spec.md` FRONTMATTER `decisions:` list. Sibling ticket specled_-ymn is CONCURRENTLY adding specled.decision.cross_vm_temp_names to that exact list. Stay out of the frontmatter so the two branches do not collide. If your work genuinely requires a frontmatter change, say so in your completion record instead of making it.
- Any other subject's spec file.
- The other specled_-xkn children's territory (26g, xkn.1, xkn.2).
- `CHANGELOG.md`, `VERSION`.

## Out of Scope (intent)

- No behavioral change to coverage closure, triangulation, or HTML rendering. This is a spec-hygiene / prose-deduplication ticket; the diff should be comments and spec prose only.
- Do not add, rename, or restate any of the 8 split requirements from specled_-q6l.5 — they are already correct and covered.
- Do not delete a covering test to simplify the repoint.

## Verification (gates)

Final tier is change-scoped. Do NOT run the full suite — whole-system proof runs at the orchestrator merge gate and PR CI.

1. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`
2. `mix test test/specled_ex/review_test.exs test/specled_ex/review/html_test.exs test/specled_ex/review/coverage_closure_test.exs test/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation_test.exs`
3. `mix spec.check --no-run-commands`.

   CORRECTION (orchestrator, 2026-07-26, after cold verification proved the original wording false): this gate does NOT catch a `# covers:` marker in `lib/**` or `test/**` that points at an unknown requirement id. A typo'd cover id in a lib marker leaves `spec.check` GREEN (verified by experiment). It only fires in the REVERSE direction — `verification_target_missing_reference`, when a spec's `covers:` list names an id that no longer appears in its target file — and only once NO valid marker remains for that id. `scenario_unknown_cover` fires for a bad id inside a SPEC verification entry, which is a different code path. So a green spec.check is NOT proof that lib/test markers resolve.
4. Execute the six spec_review verification entries you touched.
5. DANGLING-REFERENCE GATE — mandatory, and it is a GREP, not a spec.check. Because of the correction above, the only reliable check for lib/test markers is to validate every `# covers:` id in your touched files against the real requirement-id corpus by hand. After your repoint, `grep -rn coverage_tab_bind_closure .spec/ lib/ test/` must return only occurrences you deliberately kept (zero, if you deleted the compound requirement); additionally confirm that EVERY cover id you introduced resolves to a requirement id that exists. Paste both results into your completion record.
6. NO-ORPHANED-CONTRACT GATE — mandatory. If you delete or shrink a requirement statement, every normative sentence you remove must still have a home: either restated in a split requirement, or deliberately retired with that decision recorded. Deleting a `shall` sentence without restating it is spec weakening by omission and `spec.check` CANNOT see it, because it is prose. Before committing, diff the old statement against the union of the surviving statements and account for every dropped clause in your completion record. Also check `.spec/decisions/` consequence lines that depend on the sentence you removed.

Verdict: FAIL

Gaps:
- specled.spec_review.coverage_tab_bind_closure — two clauses of the newly authored statement cannot fail. The statement asserts the function returns "sorted `reached_files`, sorted `unreached_files`". I replaced both `Enum.sort()` calls with `Enum.sort(:desc)` in lib/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation.ex:227 and :230-234 and the requirement's ONLY executed verification, `mix test test/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation_test.exs`, stayed 39 tests / 0 failures GREEN. Failure mode the existing tests do not catch: `per_requirement_reach/2` could return both file lists in arbitrary or reverse order and nothing would redden, because every requirement in `fixture_closure_map/0` (coverage_triangulation_test.exs) has a single-element `closure_files`, and the only other caller (review/coverage_closure_test.exs:291) also reaches exactly one file — list order is unobservable in every fixture. The `reaching_tests` sortedness clause IS falsifiable (mutation 2, red), and the count/key/sentinel clauses ARE falsifiable (mutations 1-of-implementer and 3, red), so this is a partial not total defect — but it is exactly the pattern this epic exists to retire: normative prose newly written into a `priority: must` that no test can contradict. The implementer's own falsifiability record only exercised the `:no_coverage_artifact` head clause, i.e. the one clause that is a separate function head and the cheapest possible proof; the data-shape clauses it newly authored were never probed. Fix is small and there are two honest options: (a) give one fixture requirement a two-file closure (e.g. `closure_files: ["lib/z.ex", "lib/a.ex"]`) and assert the returned order, which makes both clauses falsifiable and is a 3-line test change; or (b) drop the word "sorted" from those two keys in the statement and keep it only on `reaching_tests`, where a test enforces it. Either closes the gap; (a) is better because the implementation does sort and callers may rely on it.

Notes (advisory only — neither changes the verdict):
- SEAM, base parity, so not a Gap: `coverage_no_debug_info_distinct_note`'s "those MFAs are not counted ... as covered" half is verified only as rendered disclaimer TEXT, not as an actual count. I patched lib/specled_ex/review/html.ex so `executed_count = length(covered) + length(no_debug)` — the renderer then reports the no-debug MFA as executed in the closure line WHILE still printing "not counted as covered or uncovered" — and `mix test test/specled_ex/review/html_test.exs` stayed 97 tests / 0 failures. html_test.exs:1391 asserts the page SAYS they are not counted, not that they are not counted. I am NOT bouncing on this: at base 402f4a27 the identical clause had the identical evidence (the same test, then attributed to the compound umbrella), so this diff neither introduced nor weakened it — it is a pre-existing test-strength gap that this ticket merely gave a proper id. Worth a follow-up ticket: add `refute html =~ "1 executed"` (or assert "0 executed") to that test.
- The third path was right and the bounce's option (a) was unachievable — stated plainly under "Umbrella falsifiability" above, repeated here for routing: `append_only.ex:114-137` would have fired `append_only/requirement_deleted` on an outright delete absent an authorizing ADR, and `.spec/decisions/` is not in this ticket's Allowed touches. The bounce should not be read as the implementer having ignored guidance.
- Subject-boundary seam, not a violation: a spec_review-subject requirement now states the return contract of a `SpecLedEx.CoverageTriangulation` function. The cross-subject binding is pre-existing (the source_file entry targeting lib/specled_ex/coverage_triangulation.ex from spec_review existed at base 402f4a27), triangulation.spec.md:219 independently blesses the function's continued existence, and triangulation.spec.md was out of scope for edits — so this was the only available home. If the epic ever revisits it, `specled.triangulation` is the more natural owner.
- `per_requirement_reach/2` has no PRODUCTION caller: only coverage_triangulation_test.exs and review/coverage_closure_test.exs:291. The statement's "that `SpecLedEx.Review.CoverageClosure` can hand to the Coverage-tab renderer" is hedged with "can", so it is not false, and the coverage_closure.ex:20 moduledoc step 4 that describes handing data into it is STALE PRE-EXISTING prose (byte-identical at base except for its `# covers:` line) describing the deleted v1 `build/2` pipeline. Not this ticket's to fix, but a `must` guarding a function with no production caller is a thin guard. Follow-up candidate.
- Untracked `.agentic-runs/` directory is sitting in the stage worktree (the implementer's log fallback after the sandbox denied `/Users/mz/.local/state/...`). It is untracked so it will not ship, and it inflates spec.check's `changed_files=7` by one. Worth removing before the merge gate so the branch-guard count matches the real diff.
